thread:
incident-bot: Pager triggered: API_GATEWAY_502_SPIKE for service=api.redwood.com region=us-west1. 502 rate > 10% over 1m, latency elevated. Escalation to oncall.

lisa: acked — I’m on it. setting status -> investigating. Can someone drop quick traffic numbers and customer impact? :phone:

matt: looking at gateway metrics now. saw error surge starting ~2601234400. 502s concentrated on /v1/generate and streaming endpoints. per-proxy: edge-fanout queue backlog rising.

raj: quick check — edge L7 proxies showing 502s from upstream timeout + upstream 502. Some 504s too. suspecting backend pool saturation on model-serving pods.

lisa: tagging product/support. @amy @support-bot — any customer reports?

amy: support-bot flagged 8 tickets in the last 5m, 2 are enterprise trial customers in EU complaining about timeouts. We should assume customer-impacted.

support-bot: Noted. Creating incident channel for external comms draft after triage.

matt: running `kubectl get hpa -n inference` — HPA at target CPU but pods are healthy, CPU ~60% on model pods. logs show repeated `upstream read timeout` from gateway -> model-svc.

raj: running a tail on edge-proxy logs: ```
[2601234410] proxy=edge-1 upstream=10.2.5.12 request="POST /v1/generate" status=502 upstream_status=504 elapsed=120s
[2601234412] proxy=edge-2 upstream=10.2.8.3 request="POST /v1/stream" status=502 upstream_error=timeout
```

lisa: hypothesis: a small subset of model-serving nodes are hitting long GC/oom or KV cache pressure causing timeouts. mitigation plan: 1) enable circuit-breaker on route to divert to backup model-variant 2) temporarily increase per-route timeout 3) scale dedicated replica group for streaming 4) notify customers. Which can we do quickly?

matt: can flip circuit-breaker for /v1/stream to fallback-variant in routing policy. pushing policy change now. command: `redwoodctl routing set --route /v1/stream --fallback model-variant-b`

raj: also enabling short-term ingress rate-limit to protect backend: `ingressctl rate-limit add api.redwood.com/stream 50r/s` — will throttle heavy clients. Doing now.

lisa: execute and monitor. Matt confirm when routing change is live.

matt: routing change applied at 2601234678. Verified: 20% of stream traffic diverted to fallback-variant, error rate on diverted traffic = 1.2%. overall 502 rate dropped to 5.6%.

amy: noting for comms: impacted customers will see degraded quality for streaming until fallback finishes warmup. drafting prod message.

lisa: good. Next: scale model-serving statefulset streaming-pool + rollout restart of the 2 suspect pods. Matt, can we restart gradually?

matt: doing a rolling restart: `kubectl rollout restart sts/streaming-pool -n inference --max-unavailable=1` — started at 2601234720.

raj: monitoring edge: 502s dipping but occasional spikes when restarts hit cold-cache. Adding temporary KV-cache warmup: prefetching common prefixes for top-20 prompt templates.

lisa: customer impact estimate? percent of overall requests affected and severity?

amy: preliminary: ~4% of total requests in us-west1, mostly streaming sessions. Two enterprise tickets high priority. We'll escalate to account teams.

support-bot: Created external status update draft: "We’re investigating elevated 5xx errors impacting streaming endpoints; mitigation in progress. More updates in 15 minutes." Ready for approval.

matt: restart progressing, 3/6 pods restarted, CPU/temp normal, downstream latency improving. 502 rate now ~2.1% in us-west1.

lisa: nice. keep circuit-breaker on for another 10m and then gradually shift back if stable. Raj keep an eye on edge queues. Amy prepare targeted customer pings.

raj: will watch edge -> alert if error rate >3% for more than 2m. Added temporary alert suppression for noisy testers.

matt: rollout finished at 2601234895. Post-restart metrics: upstream latency median down 120ms -> 30ms. No OOMs found in pod logs.

lisa: closing mitigation loop: turning down ingress rate limits and reverting routing fallback slowly: `redwoodctl routing shift --route /v1/stream --percent 80` at 2601234912.

matt: reverted to 100% primary at 2601234920. final 502 rate baseline ~0.4%.

amy: sending customer pings now: 2 enterprise recs updated; status page updated.

lisa: incident -> resolved for now. root cause: transient model-serving pod stalls causing upstream timeouts; mitigated via routing fallback, rate-limits, and rolling restart. Follow-up action items: 1) add readiness probe tuned for long GC, 2) improve autoscaling for streaming pool, 3) postmortem with deck and customer timeline. Assigning follow-up owners.

incident-bot: Incident resolved. Duration 5m13s. Tags: api-gateway, 502, streaming, mitigation, customer-impact.

support-bot: Creating postmortem draft and will collect logs + ticket list.

lisa: thanks team — please drop any logs/notes in the postmortem doc. :thumbsup:
